docs.title: Welcome to ICS4U
docs.text:
Welcome to Computer Science, Grade 12! This course builds directly on ICS3U, continuing with TypeScript and Replit as your coding environment.

Prerequisite: Introduction to Computer Science, Grade 11, University Preparation (ICS3U)

docs.title: What This Course Covers
docs.text:
This course extends the programming skills developed in ICS3U, using TypeScript as the language for building larger, more structured programs. (If your ICS3U course used a different language, that's no problem — the concepts carry over, and TypeScript syntax is introduced from the ground up in Unit 1.) You'll design software using object-oriented principles, working in a browser-based development environment (Replit) alongside a custom in-browser TypeScript runner. Through a student-managed team project, you'll apply the full software development process — planning, building, testing, and reviewing — using industry-standard project management practices. You'll also analyze algorithms for effectiveness, and examine the ethical, environmental, and career dimensions of the computer science field.

How to use this site

  • Top of the page — tabs for each unit (click one to jump in)
  • Left sidebar — once you're inside a unit, this lists every lesson in that unit
  • Right sidebar — a section index for the page you're on, linking to each heading so you can jump around within a lesson

Submit your work as instructed in D2L.

docs.title: Lesson 1: From ICS3U to ICS4U
docs.text: Welcome to ICS4U! This course builds directly on the programming fundamentals from ICS3U, so before diving into new material, let's briefly recap where you're coming from and where this course is headed.

docs.title: What You Already Know
docs.text:
Regardless of which language your ICS3U course used, you should already be comfortable with the core programming fundamentals:

  • Setting up and navigating a coding environment
  • Variables, data types, input and output
  • Selection (if/else statements)
  • Repetition (loops)
  • Arrays
  • Functions

You also learned how a computer actually runs your code — from source code, down through compiling or interpreting, to binary, to the CPU physically executing instructions. These concepts carry over completely, no matter what language you used to learn them.

Unit 2 is a deeper review

Once you've finished getting set up in this unit, Unit 2 takes a more thorough pass back through everything listed above — output, variables, data types, user input, strings, selection, loops — this time written entirely in TypeScript, with plenty of practice exercises for each topic. It also introduces a couple of things ICS3U may not have covered, like error handling with try-catch and reading/writing files. Think of Unit 2 as making sure everyone is standing on the same solid TypeScript foundation before we build ICS4U's new material on top of it.

docs.title: The Language for This Course
docs.text: This course uses TypeScript. If your ICS3U course used a different language (Python, Java, or something else), don't worry — the underlying programming concepts you already know (loops, conditionals, functions, and so on) are the same; only the syntax changes. We'll cover TypeScript's syntax and setup from the ground up in the next lesson, so no prior TypeScript experience is assumed.

docs.title: What's New in ICS4U
docs.text:
ICS4U picks up where ICS3U left off, going deeper into how real software is designed and built. Over this course, you'll build on the programming fundamentals you already know, applying them to larger, more structured programs — using TypeScript's compile-then-run workflow, which you'll learn in the next lesson.

New to TypeScript specifically?

That's completely fine. What matters coming into this course is your understanding of programming concepts in general — the TypeScript syntax itself is something we'll build together from Lesson 2 onward.

docs.title: Getting Set Up
docs.text:
The next lesson walks through setting up your Replit account, creating a project, and using the Shell — from scratch, regardless of what tools you used in ICS3U.
